summary: Nuxt: Colliding island props can share one `/__nuxt_island` path (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-46342)
details: ### Summary The fix for CVE-2026-46342 (GHSA-g8wj-3cr3-6w7v) binds each `/__nuxt_island/_.json` path to its props by hashing the `(name, props, context, source)` tuple. That hash was computed over `ohash`'s serialization, which does not escape quotes inside strings or delimiters inside keys, so two different prop objects can produce the same hash. A request with crafted props can therefore pass validation for another island's path and render different content at that path. ### Impact For example, these two prop objects serialize identically and share one island path: ```js { html: '', note: '' } { html: '\',note:\'' } ``` This reopens the scenarios described in GHSA-g8wj-3cr3-6w7v: - **`nuxt generate` / prerendering.** Nuxt caches prerendered island responses by path. If the crawler reaches a link to the colliding URL (for example in user-submitted content included in the build) before it renders the page that uses the legitimate props, the colliding response is written into the generated page. - **Path-keyed shared caches.** A CDN or reverse proxy that caches `/__nuxt_island/*` by path only, ignoring the query, can be primed with the colliding response. An attacker has to construct props that collide with a specific legitimate tuple, which in practice means at least part of that tuple is a string they control (for example a stored comment or profile field passed as a prop). Where a prop reaches an unsafe HTML sink in the island (`v-html`, `innerHTML`, a renderer treating a prop as HTML), the substituted response can execute script in the site's origin. Without such a sink, the impact is content substitution. Applications are not affected if they do not use server components or ``, or if no island receives attacker-influenced string props. Server-rendered responses that are not cached by path alone are also unaffected. ### Patches Fixed in `nuxt@4.6.4` and `@nuxt/nitro-server@4.6.4`. The island hash is now computed over a canonical JSON encoding of the tuple, in which strings and keys are escaped, so different props can no longer produce the same hash. Island hashes change as a result. Clients that build island URLs themselves should use the exported `getIslandHash` rather than hashing with `ohash` directly. Nuxt 3 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix. Upgrade to Nuxt 4. ### Workarounds - Ensure any intermediary cache keys `/__nuxt_island/*` on the full query string, not on the path alone. - Treat island props as untrusted input and do not pass them to `v-html` or other HTML sinks without sanitisation. - When prerendering, avoid including user-submitted links to `/__nuxt_island/` in crawled pages, for example by excluding that prefix with `nitro.prerender.ignore`: ```ts export default defineNuxtConfig({ nitro: { prerender: { ignore: [route => route.startsWith('/__nuxt_island/') && route.includes('?')], }, }, }) ``` ### Credits Thanks to rat5ak for reporting this issue.
